newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends lower on bearish stock data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends lower on bearish stock data.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline prices ended sharply lower Wednesday after weekly oil inventory data showed a much larger-than-expected build in gasoline stocks.

"Gasoline had been strong versus the rest of the market, but after this strong build due to high production, there was a lot of profit-taking," said Dale Wong, a senior trader at Nationsbanc-CRT in Houston.

December gasoline ended off 0.98 cent at 63.63 cents a gallon. Spread selling was also cited, with gasoline being sold to buy heating oil, which was strong after the inventory report showed a drop in distillate stocks.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday that gasoline stocks grew 4.7 million barrels for the week ended November 1. The API reported a drop of 3.8 million barrels for the week before. The market had anticipated gasoline inventory levels to remain about the same.
December crude ended five cents higher at $22.69 a barrel.

An unexpected drop in total distillate stocks, which heating oil is a component, sent heating oil prices higher. December heating oil settled 1.03 cents higher at 66.45 cents a gallon. The API said distillate stocks dropped 429,000 barrels versus estimates for a 2.5 million barrel build.
Colder temperatures expected for the large U.S. northeast market also supported heating oil prices, dealers said.

Traders said crude prices were pulled in both directions by gasoline and heating oil. Crude had risen as high as $23.15 a barrel on strength in heating oil earlier in Wednesday's session before succumbing to weakness in heat.
"We followed gasoline lower towards the end of the day. Some guys smelled blood, and new shorts have come in," said a trader of crude.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
